title: Unified storage search walks must page by cursor, not a single large Limit
answers: Why did folder tree migration validation report fake differences on large installs?
How should I fetch 'all' resources of a kind from unified storage search?
Validator says folders differ between legacy and unified storage but they don't
Search request with a huge Limit silently drops results
body:
Symptom: FolderTreeValidator reported spurious folder-tree mismatches on namespaces with many folders.
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/migrations/validator.go:buildUnifiedFolderParentMap sent a single Search with Limit: 100000; servers silently truncate at the limit, so the comparison ran against a partial folder set.
Fix pattern: page the Search request using SearchAfter set to the last row's sort values (ResourceSearchRow.GetSortFields()/ResourceTableRow.GetSortFields()), looping until a page comes back smaller than the requested page size.
Constraints: use cursor-based paging, not offset, whenever the underlying data can be created/deleted between page fetches — an offset shifts and can skip or duplicate rows; applies to any ResourceClient.Search-based 'walk everything' logic, not just folders.
applies: Any code calling resourcepb ResourceIndexClient.Search / Resource search client to enumerate an entire result set across unified storage.
says: Folder tree migration validation reports incorrect missing folder discrepancies on large accounts.
Ensure the folder migration checker successfully processes directories containing thousands of dashboard folders.
Organizations with massive folder structures see false comparison errors during storage upgrades.
The folder structure validator must inspect every nested subfolder without dropping items.
Dashboard folder verification falsely claims folder parent relationships differ after migration.
